Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Our security team is working through Redwood's responses and has two follow-ups before we can sign off on the DPA annex:

1) Can you confirm whether session-level K/V cache entries (used for inference) are treated as ephemeral and excluded from long-term backups? We need assurance we won't see persistent PII in backups.
2) We also need an audit trace mapping: for any PII-containing request, which Redwood roles/systems have read access (e.g., SRE, on-call, analytics pipeline) and under what justification/approval mechanism. HealthGrid requires a documented justification per role and a retention period for those audit logs.

Can you also attach a dataflow diagram that clearly marks egress points and any cross-border transfers?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — our procurement window is tight.

Julia —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, with attachments and a short matrix included:

1) Cache/backups: Our serving runtime maintains KV cache in-GPU and in-memory processes. We do not persist KV cache entries to long-term backups. Persistent storage only contains model binaries, metrics aggregates, and explicit customer-provided artifacts (e.g., uploaded files). Evidence: see attached "PII_dataflow_v2.pdf" (diagram page 3) which marks ephemeral vs persistent stores.

2) Access & justification: I've attached "access_matrix.xlsx" with role-level access and justifications. High-level:
  - SRE on-call: read access to serving logs and runtime metrics for troubleshooting. Access requires an approved incident ticket and is audited.
  - Platform Engineering: limited read for billing/usage; no access to raw request bodies unless a customer provides explicit consent for support reproduction.
  - Security team: read access to audit logs for investigations; access is gated via JIT (just-in-time) access requests and approval workflows.
  - Analytics pipeline: tokenized/aggregated metrics only; raw PII is filtered before ingestion.

Retention: audit logs are retained for 12 months by default; retention is configurable per contract and can be extended for enterprise customers. The "access_matrix.xlsx" contains the retention column per artifact.

Cross-border transfer: per the diagram, the control plane may route metadata (region, model id, latency stats) to control-plane regions for routing decisions; payloads with PII remain in-customer-region for Private deployments and are pinned to us-east-1 for this contract unless you opt into multi-region routing. For Hosted customers we provide routing policies; sensitive workloads can be pinned. See p.2 of the PDF for transfer rules and supported SCC controls.

Next steps I propose:
- I can prepare a one-page audit-trace narrative mapping a sample PII request to every system/role that touches it (including log locations and retention).
- Rishi (cc'd) can pull the SOC 2 artifact excerpts you requested if HealthGrid needs them in parallel.

If that works I'll send the audit narrative by EOD Friday.

Cheers,
Karthik
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
